title: A pragmatic roadmap with five priorities for public sector data sharing
gist: Public sector data sharing fails for institutional, not technical, reasons; the authors propose five priorities (clear public purpose, an anchor institution, fixing incentives, visible trust, and investing in people) to turn administrative data into a reusable governance asset.

insights.claim: Evidence shows public data-sharing initiatives can generate US$5 in social returns for every dollar invested.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Strong ROI case supports rising government spend on data infrastructure and stewardship.

insights.claim: Administrative data are gaining importance for policy against a global backdrop of declining response rates to statistical surveys.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Structural shift from surveys toward admin and alternative data benefits data-integration vendors.

insights.claim: Brazil linked health and social data across agencies and gave accredited researchers access to study policy impacts on over 100 million citizens; mobile-operator data sharing supported Nepal's 2015 earthquake relief.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Precedents for large-scale linked data and telco data monetisation for public use.

insights.claim: Most governments fail at data sharing not because they lack databases but because institutional conditions for safe, sustained sharing are weak; legacy systems accumulate undocumented tables requiring tacit knowledge.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Technology-only govtech sales underdeliver; stewardship and documentation services are the real bottleneck.
insights.quote: The data may be valuable, but it is rarely ready.

insights.claim: World Bank data governance assessments in Kerala and Mozambique found data governance is 'soft infrastructure' as much as technology; Kerala's sophisticated platforms lacked common standards, methods and policies.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Expect DFI lending to prioritise governance frameworks and standards alongside platforms.
insights.locator: Recent World Bank Group data governance assessments

insights.claim: APIs, Trusted Research Environments and interoperable standards are necessary but insufficient; data sharing must be designed as an operating model, not a one-off transaction.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Recurring-operations models (managed stewardship) beat one-off platform builds.
insights.locator: That is why public sector data sharing

insights.claim: Data sharing must be tied to a specific government priority or transformation program; vague 'share more data' mandates lose momentum and feel like administrative burden.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Look for data projects embedded in flagship reform programs; standalone ones stall.
insights.locator: 1. Start with a clear public purpose

insights.claim: National statistical offices are natural anchors for statistics and research sharing, while central digital authorities or delivery units suit operational sharing, supported by dedicated gateway teams of data engineers, metadata, legal and privacy specialists.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Identifies which agencies control procurement for data-sharing infrastructure.
insights.locator: 2. Build governance around an anchor institution

insights.claim: Public-private data partnerships, such as integrating retailers' price data into inflation statistics, and the Development Data Partnership's projects (air quality in Southeast Asia, school connectivity in Jamaica, AI talent mobility) can generate significant impact.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Private scanner/price data feeding official CPI is a growing trend relevant to macro data users.

insights.claim: Data-rich departments bear the political risk of data exposing their shortcomings plus curation costs, so mandates rarely work; a central agency should coordinate incentives such as curation grants, capacity building and core funding.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Incentive misalignment explains stalled data programs; watch for central funding lines.

insights.claim: Treating reusable linked and anonymised datasets as data infrastructure changes the investment logic, justifying stewardship funding before urgent analytical requests arrive.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Reframing data as infrastructure could unlock capex-style budgets.
insights.quote: Treating reusable data assets as data infrastructure changes the investment logic.

insights.claim: Public trust is foundational, not a communications add-on; governments should publish which data are shared, for what purposes and under which legal framework, and engage civil society to avoid building impressive but underused supply-driven portals.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Privacy backlash is the key political risk to government data programs.
insights.quote: Public trust is foundational to data sharing, not a communications add-on.

insights.claim: Capacity is the most overlooked part of data sharing; teams need specialists combining engineering, metadata, anonymisation, legal and domain knowledge to bridge researchers and operational departments.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Talent scarcity is a binding constraint; services firms supplying this skill mix face demand.

insights.claim: Neglecting metadata creation and data-quality mapping is a false economy because quality problems compound across the lifecycle to render insights partial or misleading.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Data-quality tooling is under-bought relative to its value.
insights.locator: It is also important to invest in foundational work

insights.claim: Linking tax and education data enables fine-grained, gender-disaggregated analysis reusable by local governments, planning ministries and gender agencies.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Linked administrative data is a multi-use public asset.
insights.locator: Finally, a central agency can invest

insights.claim: The cost of building a data-sharing ecosystem pales in comparison with the cost of digital transformation programs, which only pay off when data sharing is central rather than an afterthought.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Digital transformation budgets without data-sharing components carry execution risk.
insights.locator: Conclusion: data sharing is a governance reform
